html:
The Pumé, also called the Yaruro, are a people of the llanos, the wide savanna plains of Apure state in Venezuela, along the Capanaparo, Sinaruco and Apure rivers near the Orinoco.

Their language has no proven relatives. Along the rivers they fish and grow some crops, while savanna groups live mostly by foraging roots, game and fish. Anthropologists have studied them as one of the last foraging peoples of the region. Their neighbours include the Guahibo and the Achagua. Cattle ranches took much of the llanos from colonial times on.
